## Factorise fully {.psf-lesson}

Take out the highest common factor first. Use the coefficients inside the bracket for PSF.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$3x^2+9x-30$

::: {.fragment}

$=3(x^2+3x-10)$

**P** $=-10$, **S** $=3$. The number farther from zero is positive.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $-1,\ 10$ | $9$ |
| $-2,\ 5$ | $3$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Choose $-2,5$: $-2+5=3$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(x-2)(x+5)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$3x^2-9x-30$

1. Take out the common factor.
2. Identify which sign changes inside the bracket.
3. Use PSF to finish factorising.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(x^2-3x-10)$

**P** $=-10$, **S** $=-3$. The number farther from zero is negative.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $1,\ -10$ | $-9$ |
| $2,\ -5$ | $-3$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Choose $2,-5$: $2-5=-3$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=3(x+2)(x-5)$

:::
